{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./udacity_new_xml_test_train.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   -n 4           -> -n 4
#   --gres gpu:1   -> -g 1
#   --mem 30G      -> (not translated; see note)
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -g 1 --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm -p mhigh,mlow not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the mhigh/mlow partitions.

  # NOTE: Slurm -o/-e use %x/%u/%j expansions which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  # NOTE: Slurm --job-name=udacity_new_xml_test_train not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mem 30G not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  nvidia-smi
  export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1

  LEARNING_RATE=1e-3
  BATCH_SIZE=1
  DECAY_STEP=5

  # Run within the allocation. If this code expects 4 GPUs for --mGPUs, adjust GPU request accordingly.
  flux run -n 4 -g 1 python3 test_net.py --dataset pascal_voc --net res101 \
    --cuda --mGPUs --checksession 1 --checkepoch 20 --checkpoint 2504
fi
"
}
